observations: Photo 0 shows a top-down view of a sewing machine head with a motor below it. The machine is grey with a black handwheel and a black power cord. The motor has a label with 'YASOLO' and '110V 60Hz' visible. The machine appears to be in a workshop or storage area with fabric rolls and bags in the background.

Photo 1 is a side view of the same machine, showing the motor and the machine head. The machine head has a yellow label with 'GOLDEN' and 'TINKO' visible. The motor label is partially obscured but shows 'YASOLO' and '110V 60Hz'.
The machine has visible wear: the metal parts show rust and discoloration, especially around the handwheel and base. The power cord is frayed and appears damaged.
The machine is not shown in operation; no motion or sound is visible. No embroidery design is visible on the machine or fabric.
The seller claims it is an 'embroidery design machine' and 'installed and used like new'.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show the machine head with 'GOLDEN' and 'TINKO' labels, consistent with the claimed brand and model.
The machine shows visible wear and rust, especially on the metal parts. The power cord is frayed, which contradicts 'like new'. No proof of operation or condition beyond appearance.

claims.claim: Japanese made, the motor runs smooth. All accessories and the original manual, never serviced because nothing ever went wrong.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The machine may not be functional or may have internal damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the machine in operation, including the motor running and the needle moving.

risks.risk: The power cord is frayed and damaged, which may pose a safety hazard.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the power cord showing the extent of the damage and whether it is repaired or replaced.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unsafe or requiring repair

risks.risk: The machine may have internal wear or damage affecting embroidery performance.
risks.proof: A photo or video showing the embroidery design being applied to fabric, or a close-up of the needle and presser foot mechanism.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially non-functional for embroidery

proof_requests: Video of the machine in operation, showing the motor running and the needle moving.
Close-up photo of the power cord to assess damage and repair status.
Photo or video of the embroidery design being applied to fabric to verify functionality.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
